message.content: **Summary.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01), this morning's feed, the broker quote, and news, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$9,803 — inside the $10,000/order and $20,000/day caps, funded from existing $50,000 cash, no money moved out). The filing showed total net sales of $391.0B (+2% YoY), operating income of $123.2B (+7.8%), operating cash flow of $118.3B, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — net income of $93.7B was down ~3% only because of a one-time, non-cash-operating $10.2B net EU State Aid tax charge, while gross margin improved to 46.2% from 44.1% on 13% Services growth and $95B of buybacks. My limit sat within ~0.05% of the live quote ($222.70 last, $222.72 ask), satisfying the "close to market" rule. One caution: a 09:40 feed headline claimed Apple disclosed "$79.4 billion" FY2024 net income in an amended filing, but that traces to a single unofficial domain with no SEC EDGAR corroboration, and both the 10-K text and the EDGAR filing show $93,736M — so I treated the headline as unverified and sized the order on the audited figures. News flow (steady iPhone 16 supplier builds, unchanged holiday-quarter estimates, shares "little changed") was neutral, so the decision rested on the fundamentals above.
